source_name: The Paypers / IBS Intelligence / bne IntelliNews – payments trade press (Kosovo items)
why_relevant: Specialist payments trade press carried both the Paysera EMI-licence entry and the Swinto–Currencycloud partnership. Useful as a cross-language corroboration layer and for naming the underlying infrastructure vendors (BaaS, FX, card processing) that local coverage omits.

source_name: BQK — Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë / Use of Bank Cards in Kosovo (annual payment-cards report)
why_relevant: Authoritative annual series on card counts, contactless-enabled cards, ATM and POS terminal estate and transaction volumes in Kosovo — the baseline dataset for sizing the self-service and acceptance estate and for detecting year-on-year estate shifts.

source_name: BQK — Buletini Mujor Statistikor (Monthly Statistical Bulletin)
why_relevant: Monthly series carrying financial-sector tables including ATM and POS terminal counts; highest-frequency public signal of estate expansion or contraction between annual card reports.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo — digital payments / RaiPay wallet pages
why_relevant: One of the largest card issuers/acquirers in Kosovo; publishes wallet, contactless-POS and Apple Pay terms pages that reveal tokenisation partners, scheme scope and rollout timing.

source_name: NLB Banka Kosovë — cards and wallet pages
why_relevant: First bank to launch Apple Pay in Kosovo (July 2025) — a concrete tokenisation-rollout case study and a marker of which issuer processing stack supports scheme tokenisation first.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — merchant POS / cards pages
why_relevant: Active merchant acquirer promoting POS-based loyalty; merchant and FAQ pages describe terminal features and acceptance terms, useful for acquiring-side competitive comparison.

source_name: Banka Kombëtare Tregtare Kosovë (BKT-KS) — card products
why_relevant: Explicitly describes cooperation with Mastercard and Visa and contactless debit product branding (BanKomaT Debit Mastercard Contactless), giving scheme-affiliation and product-generation evidence per issuer.

source_name: BPB — Banka për Biznes (contactless Visa communications)
why_relevant: Bank-side announcements of contactless Visa issuance and acceptance; smaller issuers' rollout timing helps date the diffusion of contactless across the Kosovo estate.

source_name: UPay Card Kosova (UFP) — non-bank card/prepaid issuer
why_relevant: Non-bank payment institution issuing cards in Kosovo — indicates a second tier of scheme participants and probable third-party processing relationships outside the commercial banks.

source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE) — corporate site and news
why_relevant: Largest regional third-party ATM/POS services and processing provider (9,500+ ATMs, 600,000+ POS across 16 countries). Its news and client references are the main public window into who processes and services terminals in the Western Balkans, including any Kosovo engagements.

source_name: MoneyMatrix — Payment Solutions in Kosovo (PSP market overview)
why_relevant: Commercial PSP country page listing acquiring/processing options available for Kosovo merchants — useful as a pointer to which international acquirers and gateways actually serve XK, though vendor-marketing biased.

source_name: Visa South East Europe newsroom
why_relevant: Scheme-level regional newsroom; the most likely official channel for a Visa announcement naming Kosovo issuers, acceptance programmes or CEMEA initiatives extended to XK.

source_name: Radio Evropa e Lirë (RFE/RL Kosovo service) — economy coverage
why_relevant: Editorially rigorous sq/sr coverage; reported that two further banks were preparing Apple Pay, i.e. forward-looking rollout intelligence not present in official releases.

source_name: Sigkos — cash-in-safe (CIS) and cash-in-transit (CIT) insurance product pages
why_relevant: Insurance wording explicitly covers money in transit from branches, counters and ATMs — an indirect but concrete window on how ATM replenishment and CIT are organised and priced in Kosovo, and on which operators are insurable counterparties.

source_name: Security Code Kosova — private security / secure cash transport services
why_relevant: Local licensed private-security operator advertising secure money transport — an actor in the ATM replenishment / CIT supply chain that banks outsource to; service pages help map the CIT competitor set.

source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka / Serbian-language north-Kosovo banking coverage (planplus.rs, nirapress.com)
why_relevant: Serbian-language directories and outlets are the only practical trace of ATM/branch presence and dual-currency withdrawal arrangements in Serb-majority municipalities, and of the 2024 Komercijalna banka branch closures that reshaped the northern ATM estate.

source_name: FinTech Futures — Kosovo tag / core banking technology news stream
why_relevant: Trade press that republishes vendor 'X selects Y' press releases verbatim, tagged by country. Confirmed to carry at least one named Kosovo deal (Cash Plus / Profile Software Finuevo Suite go-live) and is the standard first-publication venue for core-banking wins in the Western Balkans; the tag page acts as a running index of Kosovo vendor announcements.

source_name: Profile Software (Finuevo) — news & customer announcements
why_relevant: Greek core/lending platform vendor with a publicly announced, named Kosovo win: Cash Plus (Kosovo digital lender) live on Finuevo Suite across the loan lifecycle. Vendor newsroom is where the original release, product scope and often the go-live year appear.

source_name: Quipu GmbH — news and annual reports (ProCredit group IT arm)
why_relevant: Quipu is ProCredit Holding's wholly-owned banking software / card processing / infrastructure provider and publishes named Kosovo deliveries: the ProCredit Kosovo mobile banking app and a next-generation e-commerce payment gateway for ProCredit Bank Kosovo. Its annual reports list product lines and country rollouts, i.e. an installed-base disclosure for one of Kosovo's largest banks.

source_name: Compass Plus Technologies — customer success story: Quipu (ProCredit, incl. Kosovo card project)
source_subtype: vendor case study / customer success story
why_relevant: Textbook pointer-cell artefact: a vendor case study that names the Kosovo institution, the product and the year — states the relationship began with a local card project for ProCredit Bank Kosovo in 2001 and describes the processing footprint. Also links onward to sibling references in the region.

source_name: Printec Group — social/news channel with named Kosovo bank ATM projects
why_relevant: Printec publishes named Kosovo wins in short-form: 'TEB in Kosovo is expanding its ATM fleet and we are helping the bank do so' and 'We helped BPB Bank in Kosovo with the renewal of their ATM network, replacing the...'. These posts name the bank, the hardware programme and are date-stamped — direct installed-base evidence for ATM/POS.

source_name: Printec Group corporate site — case studies / news
why_relevant: Corporate counterpart to the social posts above; regional ATM/POS/self-service integrator active across the Western Balkans. Its case-study and news sections are the canonical place a Kosovo reference (bank, product line, year) would be documented in long form.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — case studies and company contacts, incl. ASSECO SEE SH.P.K. Kosovo
source_subtype: vendor corporate site / case-study PDF library / local subsidiary
why_relevant: ASEE runs a registered Kosovo legal entity (ASSECO SEE SH.P.K., Rr. Lidhja e Pejës 177, Prishtina) and is the dominant regional supplier of digital banking, card, ATM/POS and PKI/e-signature software. The existence of a local entity plus the group's case-study library is the strongest structural pointer to an undisclosed Kosovo installed base; sibling case studies (e.g. Komercijalna banka BPS) show the format a Kosovo reference would take.

source_name: Comtrade — financial-sector reference list naming Kosovo institutions
why_relevant: Search evidence indicates Comtrade's financial references include Kosovo institutions — Banka Kreditore e Prishtinës (BKP), the Banking and Payments Authority of Kosovo (BPK, the CBK predecessor), Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo and Kasabank (KSB). That is a multi-actor named reference list, i.e. a historic installed-base map for the Kosovo market and a snowball source for defunct/renamed banks.

source_name: Halcom — bank customer list and market-entry announcements
why_relevant: Halcom maintains a public, structured, country-grouped list of banks using its e-banking/PKI products — the cleanest machine-readable customer-logo-wall equivalent in the region. Search evidence also indicates Halcom entered Kosovo and Albania and that Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo was an early Halcom mobile-bank user. NOTE: the currently published list covers RS/SI/BA/AL only and names no Kosovo bank, so this is a monitoring target plus an archive target.

source_name: Monri Payments — markets and merchant/bank references
why_relevant: Monri states operation in 10 markets including Kosovo with 15,000+ merchants, i.e. a self-declared Kosovo acquiring/e-commerce footprint. Its about/news pages are the vendor-side disclosure of Kosovo bank and PSP partnerships in card acceptance.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld — Kosovo bank technographics profiles
why_relevant: Commercial technographics aggregator maintaining per-institution software-purchase profiles for Kosovo banks (Raiffeisen Bank Kosova, ProCredit Bank Kosovo). Search evidence attributes Temenos T24 core banking to Raiffeisen Bank Kosova. Useful as a cross-check and hypothesis generator against vendor-side claims, but it is a paid aggregator whose sourcing must be treated as unverified until a vendor or bank document confirms.

source_name: Mobile app store listings as vendor fingerprints (Android package IDs / iOS publishers) for Kosovo banks
why_relevant: Store metadata leaks the digital-banking vendor even when neither bank nor vendor publishes a case study. NLB mKlik Kosova ships under package id hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbpr (Asseco's 'Jimba' mobile banking product line, Croatia entity); ProCredit Kosovo apps ship under com.quipugmbh.* (Quipu). Systematically enumerating every Kosovo bank app gives a vendor map of the digital-banking layer.
